clue.text: Soldier to retire in frock-and stray from path?

indicators.note: in places the turned soldier inside the garment word

parts.note: a frock is a dress

indicators.note: to retire is to fall back, so the soldier's letters run backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier quits to put on a frock and wander off the beaten track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier to retire' reads like an army man leaving service; it is the letters of the American soldier running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander away from the main subject, like leaving a path.

clue.text: Merit of French present

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
to present food is to serve it

explanation.surface: A French gift worth having.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of it, to earn it.

clue.text: Joining in play

explanation.surface: Taking part in a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining in wedlock is marrying; Getting Married is a comedy by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Formerly, a male test

parts.note: ex- means former or formerly

explanation.surface: A test that once applied to a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Bread sometimes picked up by the beak

definitions.text: Bread sometimes picked up by the beak

parts.words: Bread sometimes picked up by the beak
parts.note: bread is slang for money and the beak is British slang for a magistrate, so this is the salary some magistrates draw, not crumbs pecked by a bird

explanation.surface: A bird pecks up crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A stipendiary magistrate in Britain is a paid one, unlike unpaid lay magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular fixed salary, as paid to clergy or stipendiary magistrates.

clue.text: Home fixture in which bowler opens with hat trick

indicators.note: the bowler opens, so its first letter starts the run
a trick plays games with the letters of hat, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A cricket match on home ground where the opening bowler takes a hat-trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are misdirection: a hat-trick is three wickets with consecutive balls, and a home fixture here is a plumbing fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is a fitted item of furniture in a house.

clue.text: Tape imposing a duty?

explanation.surface: Sealing up a parcel to make it official.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding is tape or strip used to edge fabric or books; an agreement binding on someone obliges them.

clue.text: The second person is only half grand

indicators.note: only the front half of the word is kept

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand

explanation.surface: The runner-up is only worth five hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Thou is also slang for a thousand, but here it is the first four of eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the old singular pronoun of address, used for 'you' in grammar's second person.

clue.text: Wad for the hands

parts.note: hands are workers, and the wad is the money paid out to them, not padding for gloves

explanation.surface: Padding to protect the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The total wages paid to a company's employees.

clue.text: This paper factory not growing still?

parts.note: the clue appears in the Daily Telegraph
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: The newspaper's printing works has stopped expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the telegraph plant moves its leaflets visibly, so it does not keep still as it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Codariocalyx motorius, an Asian shrub whose leaflets jerk about like signal arms.

clue.text: Office fun in a TV series

parts.note: an office or post is a situation, a job
comedy is fun or humour

explanation.surface: Workplace humour in a television show, perhaps The Office itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a comic television series built around recurring characters.

clue.text: Collapse of game at home

parts.note: RU is rugby union
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home match is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is a downfall or collapse.

clue.text: Girl was unwell on the way back

indicators.note: heading backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to have ailed is to have been unwell

explanation.surface: A girl fell ill on the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Maximum temperature in freezer, ordinarily

indicators.note: in signals the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: How cold a freezer usually keeps food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a cryptic definition, but the answer sits across 'freezer, ordinarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought degrees Celsius is freezing point, the highest a freezer should reach.

clue.text: Swift attack to seize power

indicators.note: seizing grabs the power letter and holds it inside the attack

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A quick assault to take control.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast, quick.

clue.text: Western villain does not begin to make one lose one's nerve

indicators.note: not beginning drops the opening letter of the villain word

parts.note: a gunman is the bad guy of a cowboy film

explanation.surface: A cowboy baddie fails to start frightening people.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman is to deprive of courage, unnerve.

clue.text: It was John of Gaunt's precious stone

definitions.text: It was John of Gaunt's precious stone

parts.words: It was John of Gaunt's precious stone
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Richard II, Gaunt praises his country as a precious stone set in the silver sea

explanation.surface: A jewel owned by a medieval duke.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt's speech in Richard II calls his homeland 'This precious stone set in the silver sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt's famous patriotic speech celebrates his nation as a gem.

clue.text: Lear's girl left with anger, mostly?

parts.note: gone means left, departed

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter departed in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is King Lear's eldest daughter in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Power at mains switch

indicators.note: switching the letters round rearranges them

explanation.surface: Electricity at the mains switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, endurance.

clue.text: Traces of dogs?

explanation.surface: Signs that hounds have passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadows are faint traces; to shadow someone is to follow, as dogs track.

clue.text: A companion married in RADA, for example

parts.note: a crony is a close companion

explanation.surface: A partner wed at drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: RADA is formed from initials and pronounced as a word.

clue.text: We require, initially, kind of paper giving cover for the present

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words
kind of signals a loose version of paper, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: We need some paper to wrap a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping paper covers a gift, so a wrapper is a covering.

clue.text: Bird settled by Madame Tussaud?

explanation.surface: A bird paid off by the waxworks founder.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxbill is a small finch; Madame Tussaud, a waxworks maker, might pay her account in wax.

clue.text: Extortion game?

explanation.surface: Is blackmail just a sport?
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are illegal schemes such as extortion; rackets is also a court game like squash.

clue.text: Put on with new sari?

indicators.note: new letters are made from the garment word

explanation.surface: Dressing up in a new sari.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs are affected manners, pretension put on for show.

clue.text: Agent has to snoop around farm animal

indicators.note: around puts the prying letters outside the animal

parts.note: to pry is to snoop
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A spy must nose around the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is someone authorised to act for another, a representative.

clue.text: Stupendous story in the pictures

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tremendous film at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic narrative on a grand scale.

clue.text: Mark left by muffler with end cut off

indicators.note: cutting off the end removes the last letter

parts.note: a muffler is a scarf

explanation.surface: A trimmed scarf leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark a healed wound leaves.

clue.text: Ran one's hands over matted wool fabric

explanation.surface: Stroking a woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have touched or explored by touch; also a cloth made of pressed, matted fibres.

clue.text: Excessively courteous coming out of Eton service-road?

indicators.note: the letters emerge from the school's road rearranged

explanation.surface: Boys leaving Eton by the back road are too polite.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly thoughtful of others, polite to a fault.

clue.text: Decorate with spruce

explanation.surface: Smarten up with a fir tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim is to adorn with decoration; trim also means neat and smart.

clue.text: Understatement in T S Eliot play

indicators.note: playing with the poet's letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: Restraint in a drama by the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad'.
